subject: Latency fall-through & rapid capacity paths — post-demo clarifications
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Megan Li <megan@fastpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency fall-through & rapid capacity paths — recap and outstanding Qs

Hi Megan — thanks for the demo today. Quick written recap while it’s fresh and three outstanding clarifying questions so we can size the benchmark and SLO amendment correctly.

Recap (what we heard today):
- Target synchronous 95th pct latency: ~250 ms for user-facing generate calls (short chats, ≈ 32 token responses).
- Streaming / per-token requirement: steady-state token emission p95 <= 120 ms.
- Typical steady baseline: ~120 reqs/minute (2 rps) per region, but traffic pattern shows spikes up to ~3x baseline for short campaigns lasting 5–10 minutes.
- Desired behavior on burst: sub-30s scale-up to meet concurrency with acceptable queueing and fallback rules; no request loss during scale events.
- Warm-pool preference: customer prefers a small pre-warmed pool to shave cold-starts for most critical routes.

Attachments: SLO matrix and a simple warm-pool diagram attached for reference.

Outstanding clarifying questions (can you confirm):
1) For the burst profile you showed, is the 3x spike the realistic 95th pct peak or a worst-case 10x theoretical?
2) Is occasional per-request tail latency (p99) up to 800ms acceptable during peak, or must p99 also remain under 500ms?
3) Is it acceptable to fall back to a lighter quantized model variant during rapid scale events if that keeps perceived latency steady but changes output quality slightly?

Next steps I propose:
- We’ll build a short benchmark that simulates your spike profile + streaming token checks (Marissa will lead orchestration).
- Karthik will propose two warm-pool sizing options and a scale-up timeline (30s and 90s scenarios).
- We’ll schedule a 60-minute technical run next week — please confirm availability Wed/Thu.

If you can reply with the answers to Q1–Q3 and confirm Wed/Thu availability, we’ll lock in the benchmark plan.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
attachments: [slo-matrix-fastpay.xlsx, warm-pool-activation-diagram.png]

From: Megan Li <megan@fastpay.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Dunn <ops@fastpay.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency fall-through & rapid capacity paths — recap and outstanding Qs

Thanks, Olga — nice write-up and very close to what we discussed. Answers inline below.

Q1: The 3x is what we see in 95% of marketing-driven spikes. We have seen up to 8x in rare events (black-friday type), but those are single-digit occurrences per year. Treat 3x as the default spike we want SLAs around; we’ll consider 8x a separate stress-run.

Q2: p99 during short spikes: we can tolerate up to 700 ms for synchronous short responses. Streaming per-token p99 should stay under 300 ms; anything above that looks laggy to users.

Q3: We are open to a defined fallback to a smaller model variant for short windows during scale if you can quantify quality delta (we’ll want a flag in logs indicating fallback happened).

Availability: Wed/Thu next week — Wed (May 13) 10:00–12:00 PT works best for our infra folks.

Also: Alex attached a short sample of our traffic histogram (see inline reference).

—Megan
Megan Li
Head of Product, FastPay
megan@fastpay.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency fall-through & rapid capacity paths — benchmark and ops plan

On Tue, May 5, 2026 at 9:18 AM Megan Li <megan@fastpay.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Olga — nice write-up and very close to what we discussed. Answers inline below.

All — quick internal next-steps based on Megan’s replies:
- Benchmark spec: simulate sustained baseline + 3x spike for 8 minutes, plus an 8x stress run for 3 minutes (non-SLA). Include per-token timestamping for streaming. (Owner: Marissa)
- Warm-pool options: propose small (4 nodes) and medium (8 nodes) per-region warm-pool configs, with cold-start scale-up target of 30s and a degraded 90s profile for worst-case (Owner: Karthik)
- Fallback policy: create a documented fallback that selects quantized model variant and logs a fallback flag. We will include a demo of perceived output-delta on a small eval set so FastPay can sign off. (Owner: Olga + Research)
- Legal/SLA: we will draft a simple SLO amendment that references p95/p99 targets and fallback behavior. I’ll generate a draft HubSpot MAP and attach to the deal.

I’ll start the benchmark orchestration on Wed and invite FastPay to the run. Olga, please confirm you’ll send the final meeting invite for Wed May 13 10:00 PT and include the benchmark doc link. Karthik, if you can have preliminary warm-pool numbers by EOD Wed, we’ll be in good shape to present during the run.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 6 May 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency fall-through & rapid capacity paths — confirmation and next actions

Megan — thanks for the quick answers and Alex for the histogram. Confirming the plan below and next actions so we have it in writing: 

1) Technical run (benchmark) — Wed May 13 10:00 PT. Marissa will run orchestration; we’ll validate steady-state p95 <= 250 ms, streaming p95 <= 120 ms, and p99 constraints you listed. We’ll run the 3x spike profile and a short 8x stress run as a separate test.
2) Warm-pool proposal — Karthik will present small (4 node) and medium (8 node) configs and recommended activation thresholds (30s vs 90s fallbacks).
3) Fallback behavior — Redwood will implement a model-variant fallback with an audit log flag; we’ll include output-eval diffs so FastPay can approve acceptable quality deltas.

I’ve attached the SLO matrix and a simple activation diagram. I’ll also open a HubSpot MAP and a DocuSign SLA amendment for signature (link below). Please review the SLO matrix prior to the run; any changes we should make before Wed?
